author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use plain language and avoid figures of speech, idioms, and complicated metaphors.
statement: Write content at an 8th grade reading level.
audit_check: Use plain language and avoid figures of speech, idioms, and complicated metaphors.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that button, a, and label element content is unique and descriptive.
statement: Terms like “click here” and “read more” do not provide any context. Some people navigate using a list of all buttons or links on a page or view. When using this mode, the terms indicate what will happen if navigated to or activated.
audit_check: Make sure that button, a, and label element content is unique and descriptive.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use left-aligned text for left-to-right (LTR) languages, and right-aligned text for right-to-left (RTL) languages.
statement: Centered-aligned or justified text is difficult to read.
audit_check: Use left-aligned text for left-to-right (LTR) languages, and right-aligned text for right-to-left (RTL) languages.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Validate your HTML.
statement: Valid HTML helps to provide a consistent, expected experience across all browsers and assistive technology.
audit_check: Validate your HTML.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use a lang attribute on the html element.
statement: This helps assistive technology such as screen readers to pronounce content correctly.
audit_check: Use a lang attribute on the html element.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Provide a unique title for each page or view.
statement: The title element, contained in the document's head element, is often the first piece of information announced by assistive technology. This helps tell people what page or view they are going to start navigating.
audit_check: Provide a unique title for each page or view.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure that viewport zoom is not disabled.
statement: Some people need to increase the size of text to a point where they can read it. Do not stop them from doing this, even for web apps with a native app-like experience. Even native apps should respect Operating System settings for resizing text.
audit_check: Ensure that viewport zoom is not disabled.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use landmark elements to indicate important content regions.
statement: Landmark regions help communicate the layout and important areas of a page or view, and can allow quick access to these regions. For example, use the nav element to wrap a site's navigation, and the main element to contain the primary content of a page.
audit_check: Use landmark elements to indicate important content regions.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure a linear content flow.
statement: Remove tabindex attribute values that aren't either 0 or -1. Elements that are inherently focusable, such as links or button elements, do not require a tabindex. Elements that are not inherently focusable should not have a tabindex applied to them outside of very specific use cases.
audit_check: Ensure a linear content flow.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Avoid using the autofocus attribute.
statement: People who are blind or who have low vision may be disoriented when focus is moved without their permission. Additionally, autofocus can be problematic for people with motor control disabilities, as it may create extra work for them to navigate out from the autofocused area and to other locations on the page/view.
audit_check: Avoid using the autofocus attribute.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Allow extending session timeouts.
statement: If you cannot remove session timeouts altogether, then let the person using your site easily turn off, adjust, or extend their session well before it ends.
audit_check: Allow extending session timeouts.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Remove title attribute tooltips.
statement: The title attribute has numerous issues, and should not be used if the information provided is important for all people to access. An acceptable use for the title attribute would be labeling an iframe element to indicate what content it contains.
audit_check: Remove title attribute tooltips.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure there is a visible focus style for interactive elements that are navigated to via keyboard input.
statement: Can a person navigating with a keyboard, switch, voice control, or screen reader see where they currently are on the page?
audit_check: Make sure there is a visible focus style for interactive elements that are navigated to via keyboard input.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check to see that keyboard focus order matches the visual layout.
statement: Can a person navigating with a keyboard or screen reader move around the page in a predictable way?
audit_check: Check to see that keyboard focus order matches the visual layout.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Remove invisible focusable elements.
statement: Remove the ability to focus on elements that are not presently meant to be discoverable. This includes things like inactive drop down menus, off screen navigations, or modals.
audit_check: Remove invisible focusable elements.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that all img elements have an alt attribute.
statement: alt attributes (alt text) give a description of an image for people who may not be able to view them. When an alt attribute isn't present on an image, a screen reader may announce the image's file name and path instead. This fails to communicate the image’s content.
audit_check: Make sure that all img elements have an alt attribute.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that decorative images use null alt (empty) attribute values.
statement: Null alt attributes are also sometimes known as empty alt attributes. They are made by including no information between the opening and closing quotes of an alt attribute. Decorative images do not communicate information that is required to understand the website's overall meaning. Historically they were used for flourishes and spacer gif images, but tend to be less relevant for modern websites and web apps.
audit_check: Make sure that decorative images use null alt (empty) attribute values.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Provide a text alternative for complex images such as charts, graphs, and maps.
statement: Is there a plain text which lists points on the map or sections of a flowchart? Describe all visible information. This includes graph axes, data points and labels, and the overall point the graphic is communicating.
audit_check: Provide a text alternative for complex images such as charts, graphs, and maps.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: For images containing text, make sure the alt description includes the image's text.
statement: For example, the FedEx logo should have an alt value of “FedEx.”
audit_check: For images containing text, make sure the alt description includes the image's text.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that svg elements include the code focusable="false" when they are the child element of a focusable element.
statement: This prevents Internet Explorer from allowing focus to navigate through the child elements of a SVG that is meant to be decorative.
audit_check: Make sure that svg elements include the code focusable="false" when they are the child element of a focusable element.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Add aria-hidden="true" to SVG that is decorative.
statement: This is equivalent to an empty/null alt value on a non-svg image.
audit_check: Add aria-hidden="true" to SVG that is decorative.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that SVG utilizing the use element has whitespace between the svg and use elements.
statement: This solves a bug in Safari which sometimes creates hidden, unanticipated tab-stops when navigating.
audit_check: Make sure that SVG utilizing the use element has whitespace between the svg and use elements.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: It's recommended that img elements with an svg source include the role="img" attribute.
statement: VoiceOver on macOS and iOS may not correctly convey the element as an image if role="img" is not present.
audit_check: It's recommended that img elements with an svg source include the role="img" attribute.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use heading elements to introduce content.
statement: Heading elements construct a document outline, and should not be used for purely visual design.
audit_check: Use heading elements to introduce content.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use only one h1 element per page or view.
statement: The h1 element should be used to communicate the high-level purpose of the page or view. Do not use the h1 element for a heading that does not change between pages or views (for example, the site's name).
audit_check: Use only one h1 element per page or view.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Heading elements should be written in a logical sequence.
statement: The order of heading elements should descend, based on the “depth” of the content. For example, a h4 element should not appear on a page before the first h3 element declaration. A tool such as headingsMap can help you evaluate this.
audit_check: Heading elements should be written in a logical sequence.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Don't skip heading levels.
statement: For example, don't jump from a h2 to a h4, skipping a h3 element. If heading levels are being skipped for a specific visual treatment, use CSS classes instead.
audit_check: Don't skip heading levels.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use list elements (ol, ul, and dl elements) for list content.
statement: This may include sections of related content, items visually displayed in a grid-like layout, or sibling a elements.
audit_check: Use list elements (ol, ul, and dl elements) for list content.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use the a element for links.
statement: Links should always have a href attribute, even when used in Single Page Applications (SPAs). Without a href attribute, the link will not be properly exposed to assistive technology. An example of this would be a link that uses an onclick event, in place of a href attribute.
audit_check: Use the a element for links.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure that links are recognizable as links.
statement: Color alone is not sufficient to indicate the presence of a link. Underlines are a popular and commonly-understood way to communicate the presence of link content.
audit_check: Ensure that links are recognizable as links.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure that controls have :focus states.
statement: Visible focus styles help people determine which interactive element has keyboard focus. This lets them know that they can perform actions like activating a button or navigating to a link's destination.
audit_check: Ensure that controls have :focus states.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use the button element for buttons.
statement: Buttons are used to submit data or perform an on-screen action which does not shift keyboard focus. You can add type="button" to a button element to prevent the browser from attempting to submit form information when activated.
audit_check: Use the button element for buttons.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Provide a skip link and make sure that it is visible when focused.
statement: A skip link can be used to provide quick access to the main content of a page or view. This allows a person to easily bypass globally repeated content such as a website's primary navigation, or persistent search widget.
audit_check: Provide a skip link and make sure that it is visible when focused.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Identify links that open in a new tab or window.
statement: Ideally, avoid links that open in a new tab or window. If a link does, ensure the link's behavior will be communicated in a way that is apparent to all users. Doing this will help people understand what will happen before activating the link. While this technique is technically not required for compliance, it is an often-cited area of frustration for many different kinds of assistive technology users.
rationale: WCAG G201: Giving users advanced warning when opening a new window
audit_check: Identify links that open in a new tab or window.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use the table element to describe tabular data.
statement: Do you need to display data in rows and columns? Use the table element.
audit_check: Use the table element to describe tabular data.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use the th element for table headers (with appropriate scope attributes).
statement: Depending on how complex your table is, you may also consider using scope="col" for column headers, and scope="row" for row headers. Many different kinds of assistive technology still use the scope attribute to help them understand and describe the structure of a table.
audit_check: Use the th element for table headers (with appropriate scope attributes).

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use the caption element to provide a title for the table.
statement: The table's caption should describe what kind of information the table contains.
audit_check: Use the caption element to provide a title for the table.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: All inputs in a form are associated with a corresponding label element.
statement: Use a for/id pairing to guarantee the highest level of browser/assistive technology support.
audit_check: All inputs in a form are associated with a corresponding label element.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use fieldset and legend elements where appropriate.
statement: Does your form contain multiple sections of related inputs? Use fieldset to group them, and legend to provide a label for what this section is for.
audit_check: Use fieldset and legend elements where appropriate.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Inputs use autocomplete where appropriate.
statement: Providing a mechanism to help people more quickly, easily, and accurately fill in form fields that ask for common information (for example, name, address, phone number).
audit_check: Inputs use autocomplete where appropriate.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that form input errors are displayed in list above the form after submission.
statement: This provides a way for assistive technology users to quickly have a high-level understanding of what issues are present in the form. This is especially important for larger forms with many inputs. Make sure that each reported error also has a link to the corresponding field with invalid input.
audit_check: Make sure that form input errors are displayed in list above the form after submission.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Associate input error messaging with the input it corresponds to.
statement: Techniques such as using aria-describedby allow people who use assistive technology to more easily understand the difference between the input and the error message associated with it.
audit_check: Associate input error messaging with the input it corresponds to.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that error, warning, and success states are not visually communicated by just color.
statement: People who are color blind, who have other low vision conditions, or different cultural understandings for color may not see the state change, or understand what kind of feedback the state represents if color is the only indicator.
audit_check: Make sure that error, warning, and success states are not visually communicated by just color.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure that media does not autoplay.
statement: Unexpected video and audio can be distracting and disruptive, especially for certain kinds of cognitive disability such as ADHD. Certain kinds of autoplaying video and animation can be a trigger for vestibular and seizure disorders.
audit_check: Make sure that media does not autoplay.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure that media controls use appropriate markup.
statement: Examples include making sure an audio mute button has a pressed toggle state when active, or that a volume slider uses <input type="range">.
audit_check: Ensure that media controls use appropriate markup.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check to see that all media can be paused.
statement: Provide a global pause function on any media element. If the device has a keyboard, ensure that pressing the Space key can pause playback. Make sure you also don't interfere with the Space key's ability to scroll the page/view when not focusing on a form control.
audit_check: Check to see that all media can be paused.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Confirm the presence of captions.
statement: Captions allow a person who cannot hear the audio content of a video to still understand its content.
audit_check: Confirm the presence of captions.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Remove seizure triggers.
statement: Certain kinds of strobing or flashing animations will trigger seizures.
rationale: WCAG 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold
audit_check: Remove seizure triggers.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Confirm that transcripts are available.
statement: Transcripts allow people who cannot hear to still understand the audio content. It also allows people to digest audio content at a pace that is comfortable to them.
audit_check: Confirm that transcripts are available.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check your content in specialized browsing modes.
statement: Activate modes such as Windows High Contrast or Inverted Colors. Is your content still legible? Are your icons, borders, links, form fields, and other content still present? Can you distinguish foreground content from the background?
audit_check: Check your content in specialized browsing modes.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Increase text size to 200%.
statement: Is the content still readable? Does increasing the text size cause content to overlap?
audit_check: Increase text size to 200%.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Double-check that good proximity between content is maintained.
statement: Use the straw test to ensure people who depend on screen zoom software can still easily discover all content.
audit_check: Double-check that good proximity between content is maintained.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure color isn't the only way information is conveyed.
statement: Can you still see where links are among body content if everything is grayscale?
audit_check: Make sure color isn't the only way information is conveyed.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure instructions are not visual or audio-only.
statement: Use a combination of characteristics to write cues, particularly the actual names of sections and elements, rather than just descriptions like location (“on the right”) or audio (“after the tone”).
audit_check: Make sure instructions are not visual or audio-only.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Use a simple, straightforward, and consistent layout.
statement: A complicated layout can be confusing to understand and use.
audit_check: Use a simple, straightforward, and consistent layout.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure animations are subtle and do not flash too much.
statement: Certain kinds of strobing or flashing animations will trigger seizures. Others may be distracting and disruptive, especially for certain kinds of cognitive disability such as ADHD.
rationale: WCAG 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold
audit_check: Ensure animations are subtle and do not flash too much.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Provide a mechanism to pause background video.
statement: Background video can be distracting, especially if content is placed over it.
audit_check: Provide a mechanism to pause background video.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Make sure all animation obeys the prefers-reduced-motion media query.
statement: Remove animations when the “reduce motion” setting is activated. If an animation is necessary to communicate meaning for a concept, slow its duration down.
audit_check: Make sure all animation obeys the prefers-reduced-motion media query.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check the contrast for all normal-sized text.
statement: Level AA compliance requires a contrast ratio of 4.5:1.
audit_check: Check the contrast for all normal-sized text.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check the contrast for all large-sized text.
statement: Level AA compliance requires a contrast ratio of 3:1.
audit_check: Check the contrast for all large-sized text.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check the contrast for all icons.
statement: Level AA compliance requires a contrast ratio of 3.0:1.
audit_check: Check the contrast for all icons.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check the contrast of borders for input elements (text input, radio buttons, checkboxes, etc.).
statement: Level AA compliance requires a contrast ratio of 3.0:1.
audit_check: Check the contrast of borders for input elements (text input, radio buttons, checkboxes, etc.).

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check text that overlaps images or video.
statement: Is text still legible?
audit_check: Check text that overlaps images or video.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check custom ::selection colors.
statement: Is the color contrast you set in your ::selection CSS declaration sufficient? Otherwise someone may not be able read it if they highlight it.
audit_check: Check custom ::selection colors.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Check that the site can be rotated to any orientation.
statement: Does the site only allow portrait orientation?
audit_check: Check that the site can be rotated to any orientation.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Remove horizontal scrolling.
statement: Requiring someone to scroll horizontally can be difficult for some, irritating for all.
audit_check: Remove horizontal scrolling.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure that button and link icons can be activated with ease.
statement: It's good to make sure things like hamburger menus, social icons, gallery viewers, and other touch controls are usable by a wide range of hand and stylus sizes.
audit_check: Ensure that button and link icons can be activated with ease.

author: The A11Y Project contributors
title: Ensure sufficient space between interactive items in order to provide a scroll area.
statement: Some people who experience motor control issues such as hand tremors may have a very difficult time scrolling past interactive items which feature zero spacing.
audit_check: Ensure sufficient space between interactive items in order to provide a scroll area.
